texts.preamble: Ravichandra vs Satyanarayanaraju K.V on 15 April, 2025 Kabc020011162023 Before Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City Scch-25
texts.facts: The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.03.2022. 2. The petition averments in brief are as under: On 08.03.2023 the petitioner was returning to his home in his Yamaha RX135 motorcycle No. KA-06-Q-2873, when he reached near 5 th Main, Daignal Road Junction, Jayanagara 4th Block, Bengaluru, the Hond CRV Car bearing No.KA-52-P-1954 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained multiple injuries. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Promed Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 08.03.2022 to 11.03.2022 and further admitted on 27.06.2022 to 28.06.2022, undergone operations and discharged with advice to take bed rest. So far he has spent huge amount towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc., Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, running business under the name and style of "Sri Durga Mart and Events" having office at Nagasandra Circle, Basavanagudi, Bangalore. He has paid the Income Tax for the income of Rs.5,06,470/- for the assessment year of 2021-22. Due to the injury and disability he is unable to stand or walk properly. As such he is not capable of discharging his duties and thus suffered loss of income. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notices, respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements. The Respondent No.1 owner denied all the averments of the petition except admitting that his vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent as on the date of accident and the policy was valid from 01.05.2022 to 31.03.2023 as on the date of accident. The driver of the offending vehicle had a valid and effective DL to drive the aforesaid Car. Further denied the manner of accident, age, avocation, income, medical expenses etc., Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. Hence, the respondent No.1 owner prays to dismiss the petition against him. Ravichandra vs Satyanarayanaraju K.V on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167755220/ 2 The Respondent No.2 insurance company denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954. Further stated that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954. The accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself. Further stated that the petitioner was not wearing safety head gear to ride the motorcycle as on the date of accident. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. Further denied the manner of accident, age, avocation, income, medical expenses etc., Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. Hence, the respondent No.2 insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it. 5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14. Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked Ex.P.15 to 20. In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.
texts.arguments: At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that; 2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s. Ravichandra vs Satyanarayanaraju K.V on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167755220/ 4 Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others. 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
